summary: The supervision component is the oversight layer of the loop. It tracks agent runs as durable RunRecords in a RunRegistry (start/list/abort with liveness detection), drives child tasks through a Supervisor state machine with RestartPolicy and BackoffStrategy, guards flaky downstream calls with a CircuitBreaker, and watches liveness with HealthMonitor checks. It sits at the control stage: it does not do the work, it decides which runs live, restart, back off, or abort, reshaping the loop's top-level state machine and budget.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed reading src/supervision/ (run_registry, run_supervisor, mod Supervisor, circuit_breaker, health) in the context of the full engine at a ~600k budget framing, where supervision wraps the top-level Planning->Executing->Completed/Failed run.

examples.title: Register a run before it starts
examples.intent: Give every agent run a persistent, addressable identity in the RunRegistry.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Writes a RunRecord with a process-unique id at loop start, so the run is listable and abortable across restarts of the driver.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the supervision node to spawn a new run card seeded with the task and a fresh RunId.
touch_interaction.visual: A new card slides in with a spinning 'Running' badge and the pid-scoped id in monospace.

examples.mini_scenario: The user starts a task; RunRegistry.write persists a RunRecord with status Running before the executor takes its first step.
examples.pitfall: Persist the record before executing; a crash before the write leaves an untracked, unabortable run.

examples.title: List runs with liveness truth
examples.intent: Show accurate run status even when a process died without updating its record.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RunRecord.effective_status reports Stale for a Running record whose pid is gone, so the control view perceives reality, not the last write.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick down on the supervision node to refresh the run list; each card re-probes liveness.
touch_interaction.visual: Live runs pulse green, terminal runs are gray, Stale runs flash a yellow ghost badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A run's process was killed; list() calls effective_status, which sees the pid is dead and reports Stale instead of Running.
examples.pitfall: Trust effective_status over the raw field; a stored Running status can outlive its process on any platform.

examples.title: Abort a run cleanly
examples.intent: Stop a running agent and record a definite AbortOutcome.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RunRegistry.abort signals the run and transitions its RunStatus to Aborted, forcing the loop's state machine to a terminal state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press a run card to reveal an Abort action; confirm to signal the owning process.
touch_interaction.visual: The card shakes then settles into a red 'Aborted' state with a stop-hand glyph.

examples.mini_scenario: The user long-presses a stuck run; abort() returns an AbortOutcome describing whether the pid was signaled or already gone.
examples.pitfall: Handle the not-alive AbortOutcome; aborting a dead pid must update the record, not error out.

examples.title: Reclaim stale run records
examples.intent: Clean up records left Running by crashed processes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A stale record detected via effective_status is updated to a terminal status, keeping the registry an accurate ledger over many loop runs.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick a stale ghost card off the canvas to reclaim and remove it.
touch_interaction.visual: The ghost card dissolves; a small 'reclaimed' toast confirms the registry update.

examples.mini_scenario: During list, a Stale record is found and update_status marks it Failed so it no longer masquerades as active.
examples.pitfall: Only reclaim records whose pid is genuinely gone; racing a slow-starting process can kill a live run.

examples.title: Restart a failed child on policy
examples.intent: Automatically restart a supervised child that exits abnormally.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The Supervisor applies RestartPolicy to a child ExitReason, re-entering the child into the Running ChildState instead of failing the whole loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the supervisor node to expand its child tree and per-child restart counters.
touch_interaction.visual: A restarting child pulses amber then green; its restart tally increments in a corner badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A worker child panics; the Supervisor's RestartPolicy permits a restart, so it respawns and the parent loop continues.
examples.pitfall: Bound restarts within a window; unbounded restart-on-crash turns a bad child into a busy-loop.

examples.title: Back off between restart attempts
examples.intent: Space out repeated restart attempts to avoid hammering a broken dependency.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: BackoffStrategy.duration(attempt) inserts an increasing delay into the control loop before each re-spawn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the restart edge to inspect and tune the backoff curve on a mini timeline.
touch_interaction.visual: The re-spawn edge stretches longer with each attempt; a countdown ring shows the current delay.

examples.mini_scenario: The third restart of a child waits longer than the first because BackoffStrategy.duration grows with the attempt number.
examples.pitfall: Cap the maximum backoff; an unbounded curve can effectively stall the loop for hours.

examples.title: Trip a circuit breaker on failures
examples.intent: Stop calling a failing downstream after a failure threshold is hit.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CircuitBreaker moves from Closed to Open, short-circuiting subsequent calls so the loop fails fast instead of blocking.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the breaker node to see its state (Closed/Open/HalfOpen) and failure count.
touch_interaction.visual: Closed is green, Open is red with a broken-circuit icon, HalfOpen amber and probing.

examples.mini_scenario: After N consecutive endpoint failures the breaker trips Open; the next call returns immediately without touching the dead endpoint.
examples.pitfall: Count only relevant failures toward the threshold; folding user cancellations into the count trips the breaker spuriously.

examples.title: Probe recovery with a half-open circuit
examples.intent: Test whether a recovered downstream is healthy before fully reopening traffic.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After a cooldown the CircuitBreaker enters HalfOpen and allows one probe; success returns to Closed, failure back to Open.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the amber breaker to send a manual probe through the half-open gate.
touch_interaction.visual: A single probe pulse travels the edge; green settles the node Closed, red snaps it back Open.

examples.mini_scenario: The cooldown elapses, one probe call succeeds, and current_state transitions the breaker back to Closed, resuming normal calls.
examples.pitfall: Allow only one probe in HalfOpen; flooding probes defeats the point and can re-overwhelm the recovering service.

examples.title: Watch liveness with HealthMonitor
examples.intent: Continuously sample subsystem health on an interval.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: HealthMonitor runs registered checks each interval and aggregates them into OverallHealth that the control layer can act on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread the health node to fan out each registered check as its own status dial.
touch_interaction.visual: Each check dial reads Healthy/Degraded/Unhealthy; the aggregate ring shows OverallStatus.

examples.mini_scenario: The monitor ticks, GpuHealthCheck reports Degraded, and OverallHealth downgrades so the loop can shed load.
examples.pitfall: Set a sane interval and failure_threshold; too-frequent checks add overhead, too-lax miss real degradation.

examples.title: Detect a dead agent via heartbeat
examples.intent: Flag an agent that has stopped emitting heartbeats as unhealthy.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AgentHealthCheck compares last record_heartbeat against a heartbeat_timeout, transitioning the run toward abort if it stalls.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap an agent node to see its last-heartbeat age against the timeout budget.
touch_interaction.visual: A heartbeat waveform animates; when the gap exceeds the timeout it flatlines red.

examples.mini_scenario: An agent hangs and stops calling record_heartbeat; after the timeout AgentHealthCheck returns Unhealthy and the supervisor intervenes.
examples.pitfall: Emit heartbeats from the work loop, not a background timer, or a stuck worker still looks alive.

examples.title: Shed load on memory pressure
examples.intent: Degrade or pause the loop when memory crosses a critical threshold.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: MemoryHealthCheck warning/critical thresholds feed OverallHealth, letting control reduce concurrency before an OOM kills the run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the memory dial to adjust warning and critical thresholds inline.
touch_interaction.visual: The dial fills toward red as usage rises; crossing critical pulses the whole health ring.

examples.mini_scenario: Memory hits the critical threshold; MemoryHealthCheck flips Unhealthy and the supervisor pauses new child spawns.
examples.pitfall: Act on the warning tier, not just critical; waiting for critical often leaves no headroom to recover.

examples.title: Guard disk before a write-heavy act
examples.intent: Refuse write-heavy work when disk space is low.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DiskHealthCheck gates the act stage so a run that would ENOSPC is degraded before it corrupts partial output.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the disk dial before launching a build to confirm free-space headroom.
touch_interaction.visual: A fuel-gauge style dial; low free space glows red and disables the launch button.

examples.mini_scenario: Before a large artifact write, DiskHealthCheck reports Unhealthy so the supervisor blocks the act and warns the user.
examples.pitfall: Check free space, not total; a full disk on a large volume still fails the write.

examples.title: Notify the parent on child events
examples.intent: Surface child lifecycle events to the parent supervisor for oversight.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChildEvent and ParentNotification let the parent observe exits and restarts, informing higher-level control without polling.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from a child node up to the parent supervisor to route its notifications.
touch_interaction.visual: Events travel the upward edge as small pulses tinted by event type.

examples.mini_scenario: A child transitions to Terminated; a ParentNotification fires so the parent updates its aggregate view.
examples.pitfall: Do not block child progress on notification delivery; a slow parent consumer must not stall the child.

examples.title: Choose a supervision strategy for a group
examples.intent: Decide whether one failing child restarts alone or restarts the whole group.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SupervisionStrategy determines the blast radius of a failure, shaping how many children re-enter the loop on one crash.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate the strategy dial on the supervisor between OneForOne and OneForAll.
touch_interaction.visual: OneForOne highlights just the failing child; OneForAll shades the whole sibling cluster.

examples.mini_scenario: With OneForAll, one child's crash restarts every sibling to restore a consistent group state.
examples.pitfall: Match strategy to coupling; OneForAll on loosely-coupled children wastes work restarting healthy siblings.

examples.title: Build a supervisor with a builder
examples.intent: Assemble the child specs, strategy, and policy before the loop runs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SupervisorBuilder composes ChildSpecs, RestartPolicy, and parent channel into a Supervisor that defines the control substrate for the run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag child factory chips into the supervisor container to declare the tree, then tap build.
touch_interaction.visual: Dropped children snap into a tree layout under the supervisor with connecting spokes.

examples.mini_scenario: The builder adds two children with a shared RestartPolicy, then build() produces the Supervisor and its handle.
examples.pitfall: Configure strategy and policy before build; the tree is fixed once built and cannot be re-wired live.

examples.title: Read circuit breaker metrics
examples.intent: Expose breaker success/failure counts for oversight dashboards.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CircuitBreakerMetrics feed observability so the control layer can see how close a downstream is to tripping.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread the breaker node to reveal a sparkline of recent successes and failures.
touch_interaction.visual: A rolling bar chart of green successes and red failures with the current state overlaid.

examples.mini_scenario: Metrics show failures climbing toward the threshold; an operator preemptively scales the downstream before it trips.
examples.pitfall: Read metrics as a snapshot; they lag live state, so do not gate control decisions solely on stale counters.

examples.title: Map RunStatus to loop terminality
examples.intent: Know when a run has definitively finished.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RunStatus.is_terminal tells the control loop whether to keep supervising or release the run's resources.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a run card to see whether its status is terminal and eligible for cleanup.
touch_interaction.visual: Terminal cards dim and gain a checkmark or cross; active cards stay bright.

examples.mini_scenario: A run reaches Completed; is_terminal returns true so the supervisor stops probing its liveness.
examples.pitfall: Only Completed/Failed/Aborted are terminal; treating Running or Stale as terminal drops still-live oversight.

examples.title: Confirm a pid belongs to selfware
examples.intent: Avoid signaling an unrelated process that reused a recorded pid.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: pid_is_selfware verifies ownership before abort, preventing the control layer from killing a foreign process.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press abort to run an ownership check before the signal is sent.
touch_interaction.visual: A shield check flashes green before the abort proceeds, or red to cancel it.

examples.mini_scenario: An abort targets a pid that the OS recycled; pid_is_selfware returns false so the supervisor skips the signal and just marks the record.
examples.pitfall: Always verify ownership before signaling; recorded pids can be reused by unrelated processes after death.

examples.title: Expose a health endpoint for external oversight
examples.intent: Let an orchestrator poll the loop's health from outside.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: maybe_start_health_endpoint and set_global_healthy publish OverallHealth so external supervision can decide to restart the whole run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the endpoint node to copy its probe URL or toggle the global healthy flag.
touch_interaction.visual: A signal-tower icon broadcasts green when healthy, red when the global flag is down.

examples.mini_scenario: An external orchestrator polls the health endpoint; a red response triggers it to restart the selfware run.
examples.pitfall: Keep the global healthy flag honest; leaving it true during a known-bad state hides failures from external oversight.

examples.title: Compose supervision as the loop's control shell
examples.intent: Wrap the whole Planning->Executing->Completed loop in registry, supervisor, breaker, and health.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Layers RunRegistry (identity), Supervisor (restart), CircuitBreaker (fast-fail), and HealthMonitor (liveness) around the run so oversight is continuous end to end.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch to collapse the four supervision sub-nodes into one oversight shell around the run.
touch_interaction.visual: Collapsed it draws a containing ring around the whole loop with a composite status badge; spread reveals registry, supervisor, breaker, and health.

examples.mini_scenario: A run starts (registered), a child crashes (restarted with backoff), the endpoint flaps (breaker trips), and memory spikes (health degrades) all under one oversight shell.
examples.pitfall: Order the layers: identity first, then supervision and breaker, with health cross-cutting; a breaker without a registered run cannot be attributed.
